advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Handle the missing/failed-backup case in mcp_flip_upstream so a reload failure never leaves the include pointing at a to-be-removed container (fail before mv if no backup could be made, or explicitly re-derive/blank the include on restore).
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:379: `  cp "$MCP_UPSTREAM_FILE" "$bak" 2>/dev/null || true`
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:382-384: `if ! nginx -t ... ; then` / `[ -f "$bak" ] && mv "$bak" "$MCP_UPSTREAM_FILE"` — restore is conditional on a bak that a swallowed cp failure never created
autodeploy.sh:677-680: on flip failure the caller removes the new container, so a non-restored upstream points at nothing
advisory.finding: mcp_flip_upstream swallows any failure of the backup copy (`cp ... || true`), then restores only `[ -f "$bak" ]`. If MCP_UPSTREAM_FILE did not exist (or was unreadable) before the flip, no backup is written; the `mv` still installs the NEW server line, and a subsequent `nginx -t`/`reload` failure returns 1 WITHOUT restoring — leaving the include pointing at the new port. The caller then `docker rm -f`s the new container, so /mcp is left pointing at a removed backend rather than being rolled back.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In mcp_retire_sweep, only reap on an EXPLICIT exited/false inspect result; treat an empty/failed `docker inspect` as unknown-and-skip rather than as exited.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:409: `if [ "$(docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' "$n" 2>/dev/null)" = "true" ]; then`
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:417-418: `else` branch runs `docker rm "$n"` for anything not proven Running=true
advisory.finding: mcp_retire_sweep classifies containers as running vs exited by `[ "$(docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' "$n" 2>/dev/null)" = "true" ]`. Any inspect failure (transient daemon error, race where the name just disappeared) yields an empty string, which is NOT equal to "true", so control falls into the `else` branch and issues `docker rm "$n"`. An inspect error is thus indistinguishable from a genuinely-exited container, so a running container whose inspect momentarily fails is (attempted to be) reaped.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Close the deploy lock FD in the backgrounded retire subshell (e.g. `( exec 9>&-; docker stop --time "$MCP_STOP_GRACE" "$1" ) &`) so the detached `docker stop` does not keep the flock held past tick exit and block subsequent ticks.
evidence: Shared resource: the single-flight deploy lock — `exec 9>"$LOCK"` then `flock -n 9 || { log "another deploy holds the lock; skipping"; exit 0; }` (infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:429-430)

Second executor: `mcp_retire_graceful()` spawns a DETACHED child that outlives the tick — `( docker stop --time "$MCP_STOP_GRACE" "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 ) &` (infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:396); MCP_STOP_GRACE defaults to 1260 (infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:129) and is passed as `--stop-timeout`/`--time`

Interleaving window: the detached subshell inherits FD 9 (bash does not close it — a repo search for `9>&-` returns no matches, and the subshell has no `9>&-` redirect), so it holds the advisory flock open until `docker stop` finishes; meanwhile the next timer-fired tick reaches `flock -n 9` (infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:430) and fails to acquire

Sibling discipline this violates: the design deliberately releases the flock promptly rather than holding it across a wait — 'is free, whereas sleeping would hold the deploy flock for the whole wait' (infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:516), and 'flock: overlapping timer fires never overlap' (infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:34)

Concrete harm: after an mcp cutover, every subsequent tick for up to ~1260s hits `flock -n 9` -> `exit 0` 'another deploy holds the lock; skipping', so review-bot deploys, mcp deploys, disk-pressure reclaim, and the mcp retire-sweep are all blocked and `main` convergence stalls for the entire graceful-drain window (>10x the 120s timer period)
advisory.finding: The backgrounded graceful-retire subshell `( docker stop --time "$MCP_STOP_GRACE" "$1" ) &` inherits the deploy lock file descriptor (FD 9 from `exec 9>"$LOCK"`) and never closes it, so it keeps the `flock` held after the tick exits — for up to MCP_STOP_GRACE=1260s — causing the next timer ticks (every ~120s) to fail `flock -n 9` and silently no-op, blocking deploys/convergence for the whole drain window rather than releasing the lock at tick exit as designed.
scenarios: An mcp blue-green cutover completes and retires an old container that drains slowly (a busy MCP server draining toward the 1260s grace); every autodeploy tick during that drain skips, so an urgent fix-forward on `main` cannot deploy until the old container exits
advisory.suggested_fix: In `mcp_retire_graceful`, close FD 9 in the subshell before exec'ing docker: `( exec 9>&-; docker stop --time "$MCP_STOP_GRACE" "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 ) &` — the child then no longer holds the deploy flock, so the next timer tick can acquire it while the drain continues in the background as intended.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconsider `--restart always` on transient blue-green mcp containers (use `--restart unless-stopped` or `no`, and ensure reaping handles restart-on-reboot).
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:347-348 `docker run -d --name "$1" \` / `--restart always \`

`docker stop` (autodeploy.sh:396) suppresses restart-always only until the daemon restarts; on daemon/host restart docker re-launches restart:always containers that were last running, so a not-yet-reaped or overlap container comes back on its A/B host port outside the managed flow
mcp_retire_sweep only reaps EXITED containers (autodeploy.sh:417-418); a container docker restarts on boot is Running again and is no longer reaped
advisory.finding: Blue-green mcp containers are started with `--restart always`, so on a docker daemon restart or box reboot every still-present managed container (an in-overlap blue+green pair, or an old container that was `docker stop`ped but not yet reaped) is restarted by docker, defeating retirement and reintroducing containers the pointer-swap/retire logic assumed gone — a drift/idempotency and blast-radius hazard.
scenarios: Box reboots (or dockerd restarts) mid-overlap or before an old container finishes draining
An old container never drains, is `docker stop`ped, then the host reboots and docker restarts it
advisory.suggested_fix: Start blue-green containers with `--restart unless-stopped` (or `no`) rather than `always`, so a gracefully-stopped/retired container is not resurrected by dockerd on reboot; only the elected live backend should carry a persistent restart policy.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Build/tag the mcp image under an autodeploy-owned name (not the shared `compose-mcp:latest`) so a compose recreate cannot adopt an un-health-gated image on host 8091.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:629 `if ! ( cd "$COMPOSE_DIR" && docker compose build mcp ); then`
autodeploy.sh:632 `docker tag "$MCP_IMAGE" "$MCP_IMAGE:$TARGET"` — the immutable tag is derived, but the mutable `compose-mcp:latest` is what compose-up resolves
docker-compose.yml:319-323 the `mcp:` service builds `compose-mcp` and is what `compose-up.sh` brings up as compose-mcp-1
autodeploy.sh:619 declares 'blast radius = mcp containers + /mcp nginx upstream only', but a mutated latest tag reaches the compose backend too
advisory.finding: `docker compose build mcp` rebuilds and re-tags the shared `compose-mcp` (`:latest`) image that the compose-managed boot backend `compose-mcp-1` resolves by name; a subsequent `docker compose up` (e.g. compose-up.sh at boot) would recreate `compose-mcp-1` from whatever SHA autodeploy last built, bypassing the health-gated blue-green cutover — an unmanaged deploy path outside the declared blast radius.
scenarios: compose-up.sh re-runs at boot / operator runs `docker compose up -d`
A shared src/rebar change advances the build; later compose recreate adopts the newer, un-health-gated image on host 8091
advisory.suggested_fix: Build to a dedicated tag (e.g. `docker build -t rebar-mcp-autodeploy:$TARGET ...` or `docker compose build` then immediately re-tag only the SHA tag and avoid leaving `compose-mcp:latest` pointing at the new build) so the compose-managed 8091 backend's `:latest` reference is never mutated by autodeploy.

evidence: autodeploy.sh:421-424: `count="$(mcp_managed -a | grep -c . || true)" ... if [ "$count" -gt "$MCP_RELEASES_CAP" ]; then marker AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP over-cap "managed mcp containers=$count > cap=$MCP_RELEASES_CAP; ..."`

test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py:572-618: the two no-op-tick sweep tests seed only 2 managed containers each (rebar-mcp-live-8092 + rebar-mcp-old-8091; rebar-mcp-a-8092 + compose-mcp-1), never exceeding cap=3

test_both_ports_busy_does_not_start_a_third_container asserts AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP from the deploy block (reason 'port-exhausted'), which is a different code path than mcp_retire_sweep's 'over-cap' branch
ABSENCE: no test seeds >MCP_RELEASES_CAP managed containers and asserts the sweep emits the over-cap marker
advisory.finding: The mcp_retire_sweep over-cap branch — which emits AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP with reason 'over-cap' when the count of managed containers exceeds MCP_RELEASES_CAP (default 3) during a sweep — is newly added and untested. The port-exhaustion test only exercises the SEPARATE deploy-block marker (reason 'port-exhausted', emitted when mcp_free_port returns empty), not this sweep branch. A named violating input: seed 4 managed rebar-mcp containers (e.g. compose-mcp-1 plus three rebar-mcp-*-<port>) and run a no-op tick — the sweep's `count > cap` guard fires but no test asserts the marker is emitted there.
scenarios: A no-op tick with 4+ un-reaped/draining rebar-mcp containers pinning the port pool
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that seeds four managed containers (one live, three draining/running non-live) on an up-to-date tick and asserts `_markers(result, 'AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP')` contains an 'over-cap' line, distinct from the port-exhausted deploy-block path.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an auth-enforcing readiness assertion (e.g. an unauthenticated /mcp request must return 401) to the blue-green promotion gate so a code-level auth regression cannot be flipped live behind an auth-independent /health check.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:665 `curl -fsS -m 3 "http://127.0.0.1:${mcp_newport}/health"` is the sole readiness signal before the flip
autodeploy.sh:344-345 comment: `/health is auth-independent and would not catch a wrong REBAR_MCP_AUTH_*/ALLOWED_HOSTS`
docker-compose.yml:344 `# Auth ON at /mcp (static bearer). /health stays unauthenticated (custom route).`
MCP_PATHS='src/rebar ...' (autodeploy.sh:150) so any src/rebar code change triggers the mcp deploy

Partial mitigation: mcp_server.py:598-599 build_server raises AuthConfigError (fail-closed) for a MISCONFIGURED auth composite before the HTTP bind, so a config error crash-loops and fails the gate; the residual gap is an auth-LOGIC regression that still boots healthy, which only the static test_docker_run_matches_compose_mcp_service env-parity test guards (env drift, not code).
advisory.finding: The mcp blue-green promotion gate flips the public /mcp nginx upstream to a new container after only a /health check, which the code and comments explicitly document as auth-independent. Because the mcp target triggers on any shared src/rebar change, a code-level auth regression that still boots and serves /health (but no longer enforces the /mcp static-bearer / DNS-rebinding guard) would pass the gate and be promoted live. The only compensating control is a static env-parity test that cannot detect auth-logic regressions.
scenarios: A src/rebar change subtly weakens the /mcp auth middleware while /health still returns 200; the new container passes the readiness loop and is flipped live at the public edge with weakened auth.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the backgrounded `docker stop` in mcp_retire_graceful survives the oneshot tick (e.g. `setsid`/`systemd-run --scope`, or set KillMode=process / an ExecStop drain) so the full graceful grace actually elapses.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:396: `  ( docker stop --time "$MCP_STOP_GRACE" "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 ) &`
infra/systemd/rebar-autodeploy.service:20: `Type=oneshot` with no `KillMode=` override (defaults to control-group, which kills descendant processes when the main process exits)
comment at autodeploy.sh:392-393 asserts 'Issued in the BACKGROUND so the tick NEVER waits on the drain' — but a backgrounded child under a oneshot control-group does not outlive the tick
dropped.finding: The graceful retire `docker stop --time 1260` is launched as a backgrounded subshell (`( ... ) &`) with no setsid/disown/nohup, but rebar-autodeploy.service is `Type=oneshot` with the systemd default `KillMode=control-group`. When autodeploy.sh (ExecStart) exits at the end of the tick, systemd tears down the whole control group and kills the still-running backgrounded `docker stop` client, so the intended off-critical-path graceful self-drain (up to 1260s) is truncated to whatever time remains in the tick — the very SIGKILL-of-an-in-flight-op outcome (bug 7b4a) the design exists to avoid.
dropped.suggested_fix: Detach the stop from the unit's control group — e.g. `setsid docker stop --time "$MCP_STOP_GRACE" "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 &` combined with `KillMode=process` on the service, or run it via `systemd-run --scope --unit=mcp-retire-$1`.

evidence: infra/scripts/observability.sh:339-341: `publish_autodeploy_marker_delta '^AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP \{' mcp_retire_cap ...` and `'^AUTODEPLOY_MCP_MEM_ABORT \{' mcp_mem_abort`
Producer format autodeploy.sh:206: `marker() { printf '%s %s\n' "$1" "$(python3 -c ...)" ...` — token, space, JSON object
search of tests/ for `publish_autodeploy_marker_delta` returns (no matches); the marker-delta consumer path is untested for the new tokens
The bluegreen tests assert the marker is EMITTED (test file lines 379/428) but nothing asserts observability.sh's grep anchor matches that emitted line
dropped.finding: The new observability.sh marker-delta publishers for mcp_retire_cap / mcp_mem_abort — including their record-anchored ERE grep patterns '^AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP \{' and '^AUTODEPLOY_MCP_MEM_ABORT \{' — have no test. autodeploy's marker() emits the token followed by a SPACE then '{' (autodeploy.sh:206 `printf '%s %s\n'`), and the alarm pipeline depends on the observability grep anchor matching that exact producer format; nothing exercises the coupling. A drift on either side (marker format change, or a mismatched anchor) would silently break the CloudWatch counter with no failing test.
